title: A Smooth Nonquadratic Entire Affine Maximal Graph in Dimension Ten
main_claim: There is a smooth, nonquadratic u on R^10 with positive definite Hessian at every point that solves the affine maximal equation U^{ij} D_ij (det D^2u)^{-11/12} = 0. It is u = sqrt(F(|x|)^2 + t^2), where F and P come from a radial ODE system whose global existence follows from a forward-invariant box.
coverage:
I checked every step by hand.
(1) Reduction (Prop 2.1): the Hessian formula for sqrt(F^2+t^2); the unimodular basis X_i = e_i + zeta F_i e_t, which makes D^2u block-diagonal; det D^2u = F^{m+2} u^{-(m+3)} det H; w = P(1+zeta^2)^{k/2}; D^2zeta(X_i,X_j) = -zeta F_ij/F; the trace identity; and (1+z^2)h'' - m z h' = k h when k = m+2.
(2) Radial reduction to (y^{m-1}P')' = -k r^{m-1} P^{1-gamma}.
(3) Local lemma: the averaged q, j in s = r^2/2, the contraction, smoothness by induction, and the values q(0)=1, j(0)=1/m giving D^2P(0) = -11/9 I.
(4) Autonomous system: I re-derived the equations for A, B, C and D = C/B, including the (1-gamma)BD^2 term.
(5) Box: V(9/2, 7/2, 33/7) = 0 exactly. All cross-derivatives are nonnegative, so the system is cooperative and each upper face is controlled by that corner. The lower-face signs are right, and the projection/Gronwall invariance argument is valid (squared distance to a convex set is C^1).
(6) Continuation: the bounds on F, y, P and P' keep the solution in a compact set, so it extends to all r > 0.
(7) Smoothness and nonquadraticity: F >= 1 and u(0,t) = sqrt(1+t^2).
Numerically (scipy), the trajectory starting near (0,1,0) stays inside the box and tends to the corner, as the proof predicts.
sibling_notes: Consistent with the companion paper on the affine Bernstein theorem in dimensions 3-9 (rank 399, no gap). This paper is self-contained and does not depend on the companion; it cites Trudinger-Wang only for background and for the singular example.
